title: The model said it passes
scenario:
A bike-share app is getting a new look. A teammate asked a model to review three colour pairs against WCAG 1.4.3, Level AA. You check the review before the release. The colours come from the token file.

Use the exhibit. The app, the pairs and the review are made up for this case. The rule and the vendor details are from the W3C, Anthropic and OpenAI pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
PAIRS (from the token file, made up)

  A. caption      #6e7a74 on #ffffff   14px regular
  B. page title   #3a9a6a on #ffffff   24px regular
  C. SALE banner  #ffffff on #f08a24   16px bold

MODEL REVIEW (made up)
  A. "About 4.5:1. Passes AA."
  B. "About 3.5:1. Fails AA, needs 4.5:1."
  C. "About 2.5:1. Our brand guide sets this orange,
     so it does not need to pass."

OUR SCRIPT (W3C formula, no rounding)
  A. 4.469:1
  B. 3.494:1
  C. 2.510:1

TEAM PLAN
  D. "From next week, we send screenshots of each screen to a
     vision model and ask it for the contrast."

questions.prompt: Pair A: the model says it passes. What is right?

options.text: It passes, because 4.469 rounds up to the 4.5:1 line
options.explanation: The W3C guide says computed values should not be rounded. 4.499:1 would not meet 4.5:1, so 4.469 does not either.

options.text: It passes, because 14px caption text only needs 3:1
options.explanation: Large text is at least 18 point or 14 point bold, about 24px or 18.5px bold. 14px regular is not large.

options.text: It fails: 4.469 is under 4.5:1, and the line is not rounded
options.explanation: Right. Normal text needs at least 4.5:1, and the W3C guide says not to round the computed value.

options.text: It fails, because grey text is never allowed on a white page
options.explanation: No colour is banned. The rule is a number: 4.5:1 for normal text, computed without rounding.

questions.prompt: Pair B: the model says the 24px title fails. What is right?

options.text: It passes: 24px is about 18 point, large text, so 3:1 is enough
options.explanation: Right. The W3C guide says 18pt is about 24px, and large-scale text needs at least 3:1. 3.494 is over it.

options.text: It fails: every heading needs 4.5:1, whatever its font size
options.explanation: The W3C sets a lower line for large-scale text: at least 3:1.

options.text: It passes: page titles are decoration, so no contrast is needed
options.explanation: A page title gives information. Only pure decoration and other incidental text are exempt.

options.text: It fails: large text needs 3:1 only when the text is also bold
options.explanation: Large is at least 18 point, or 14 point when bold. 24px regular is about 18 point.

questions.prompt: Pair C: the model says the brand guide excuses the orange. What does the W3C guide say?

options.text: Brand colours are exempt when a written brand guide sets them
options.explanation: The W3C guide says text with low contrast due to brand guidelines is not exempted, beyond logos.

options.text: Only logo text is exempt; a brand colour does not excuse SALE
options.explanation: Right. Text in a logo or brand name has no requirement, but other text is not exempted by brand guidelines.

options.text: Bold text at 16px counts as large, so 2.5:1 is enough here
options.explanation: Large bold text starts at 14 point, about 18.5px. And 2.51 is under 3:1 anyway.

options.text: Banner text is incidental, so it has no contrast rule at all
options.explanation: SALE gives information to the reader. Incidental text is decoration, inactive or not visible.

questions.prompt: Plan D: screenshots to a vision model. What is the better plan?

options.text: Keep it, but send bigger screenshots so the model reads them
options.explanation: Bigger images can help a model read, but the W3C guide says to check the defined colours, not text as shown on screen.

options.text: Keep it, and ask two models so that a mistake is outvoted
options.explanation: Both vendors say vision models can make mistakes. Two guesses are still not the formula.

options.text: Run the formula on token pairs; use the model to list pairs
options.explanation: Right. The W3C guide says to use colours from the markup and stylesheets, and both vendors warn that vision can be wrong.

options.text: Drop checks and trust the brand guide to choose safe colours
options.explanation: The W3C guide says brand guidelines do not exempt text from the rule. The pairs still need a check.
